# Isolde Pembroke

## Overview

- **Age:** 13  <sub>[v1 c26 P4](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0004)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c2 P62](../source/v01-c02.md#nw-v01-c02-p0062), [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v1 c38 P41](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0041)</sub>
- **Origin:** Pear Hill  <sub>[v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Izzy  <sub>[v1 c18 P25](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0025)</sub>

## Appearance

Isolde is an exceptionally attractive young girl with dark eyes and shiny black hair that she inherited from her mother, along with rosy cheeks and a cheerful look passed down from her father. Outdoors, she makes a bright small figure in her crimson ulster. Nell envisions her looking gorgeous and majestic like a monarch when dressed up in white.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c15 P22](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0022), [v1 c15 P96](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0096), [v1 c25 P40](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0040)_

## Personality

Isolde is a sweet, cheerful, and good-natured girl who acts as a loyal and comforting companion. She possesses strong principles, refusing to snitch on her friends or accept blame solely on others, though she is demure and obedient toward her mother's authority. She is passionate about music and reading, though she occasionally worries about her figure.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P22](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0022), [v1 c17 P29](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0029), [v1 c19 P70](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0070), [v1 c19 P83](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0083), [v1 c21 P17](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0017), [v1 c33 P13](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0013)_

## History

Isolde Pembroke grew up at Pear Hill and became the bosom friend and schoolmate of Nell Harcourt after returning from a visit to her aunt in Delford. The pair spent their days playing at their playhouse, Larkrise, and sharing a seat at school. When Mrs. Pembroke temporarily forbade Isolde from playing with Nell after an accidental drunkenness incident involving currant wine, Isolde loyally sent Nell secret gifts and notes. After the misunderstanding was resolved, their close bond resumed, including shared adventures, school recitations, writing club activities, and a trip to town to visit her Aunt Lavinia for the Exhibition. Though Isolde was not enrolled in the Regent's entrance class alongside Nell, she remained Nell's most devoted companion, comforting her through hardship and continuing their close friendship.

_Sources: [v1 c8 P37](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0037), [v1 c12 P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 c12 P35](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0035), [v1 c13 P13](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0013), [v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c16 P42](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0042), [v1 c17 P29](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0029), [v1 c18 P43](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0043), [v1 c26 P23](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0023), [v1 c29 P11](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0011), [v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v1 c37 P21](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0021)_

## Quotes

> A joke is all it is intended to be. And you shouldn't feel so certain that a time will never come when your name is scribbled somewhere. Wilfred Mott is completely infatuated with you. It was to his mother—take note, his mother—that he declared you were the cleverest female student in the whole school. Having that said about you surpasses being attractive.  <sub>[v1 c15 P22](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0022)</sub>

> Every one of those Tulk girls acts dishonestly. Yesterday, Tibby Tulk literally set her milk bottle where mine belonged in the brook. Can you imagine? Now I refuse to talk to her.  <sub>[v1 c15 P26](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0026)</sub>

> Nell Harcourt, I am not a snitch, and besides, the fault was equally mine.  <sub>[v1 c19 P70](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0070)</sub>

> It’s going to be good, no doubt. I’m certain that portion of the one you prepared which we ate for lunch at Larkrise a fortnight back was absolutely splendid.  <sub>[v1 c21 P17](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0017)</sub>

> You have such a stylish quality, Nell. The way you carry your head gives you quite an air. My guess is it comes from your figure. Me, I am merely a dumpling. It has been a constant fear of mine, and now my suspicion is confirmed. Oh well, I guess I must simply accept it.  <sub>[v1 c33 P13](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0013)</sub>
